citation.title: Enabling integrated AI control on DIII-D: a control system design with state-of-the-art experiments
citation.authors: A. Rothstein, H.J. Farre-Kaga, J. Butt, R. Shousha, K. Erickson, T. Wakatsuki, P. Steiner, S.K. Kim, A. Jalalvand, E. Kolemen

topic: DIII-D plasma control system framework (PACMAN) for deploying ML models and controllers
own_question: How can a modular real-time PCS framework be designed to host diverse ML predictors and controllers on DIII-D?
actual_method_and_evidence: The paper describes the design of a four-block architecture: inputs, models, controllers and actuator outputs. It reports five DIII-D applications at the level of deployment description, with per-application model and controller compute times (Table 2). The extracted text does not evaluate KSTAR data, CES nowcasting, or the temperature of impurity ions. Table 1 lists inputs such as CER profiles at a 20 ms profile-fitting timescale and BES/ECE at 0.001 ms. These are framework entries, not measured arrival latencies.
input_target_timing_if_relevant: The source states only that the profile-fitting update timescale for CER-derived Ti is about 20 ms on DIII-D (Table 1). It does not measure actual report availability delays. That timing should not be transferred to KSTAR CES.
validation_if_relevant: There are no held-out validation designs. The experiments are described as successful demonstrations without a quantitative comparison relevant to our paper.
forbidden_inferences: Do not infer KSTAR CES latency or arrival times from DIII-D Table 1.
Do not claim the source shows a deployment path or benefit for our offline estimator.
Do not treat the 20 ms CER fitting timescale as main-ion or physical truth.
Do not cite it as evidence that our nowcast is real-time capable.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: The paper is a DIII-D control-infrastructure paper. It could support, at most, an optional applications remark that ML-model deployment frameworks exist on another device. It gives no evidence on causal CES nowcasting, KSTAR, or the incremental value of BES/ECEI. Citation is optional and only in an applications or outlook context. Our paper has no implemented deployment, so this source carries no claim for our results.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
